memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not give any of your children to be sacrificed to Molek, for you must not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.'" - Lev 18:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the middle of this chapter comes the most horrifying verse in it. Canaanite religion included child sacrifice — parents giving their own children to the fire in hope of favour from a god.

God forbids it absolutely. And the reason He gives is striking: you must not profane the name of your God. To do this would be to say something false about who He is.

Because this is the deepest lie about God — that He is the kind of deity who demands your children.

Look at what the true God actually did. When Abraham raised the knife over Isaac, God stopped him and provided a ram instead (Gen 22:12-13). He did not want the boy.

And then, at the cross, God did not demand a child from us. He gave His own. He who did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all (Rom 8:32).

Every false god demands. The true God provides.

We do not have Molek. But we can still treat children as currency — sacrificing them to our ambition, our schedules, our need to be seen as successful. Children are a heritage from the LORD (Ps 127:3), not an investment.

Are you giving your children anything to a god that will not love them?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What do false gods demand, and what does the true God give?
2. Are you sacrificing time with your children to something that promises success?
3. How does Romans 8:32 change your view of God's heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are not a God who demands my children but One who gave Your own Son. Guard me from sacrificing what matters most to things that cannot love me. Amen.
